security_audit.summary: Static findings are mostly safe HubSpot integration examples, including official OAuth endpoints and named environment variables. I found no evidence of malicious data exfiltration or prompt injection. One content issue remains because the webhook validation example mixes v3 headers with v2-style signature logic.

remediation.issue: Webhook signature validation guidance is inconsistent.
remediation.suggestion: Update the webhook section to implement HubSpot v3 signing exactly, include the timestamp in signed data, and use constant-time comparison.

semantic_findings.title: Inconsistent Webhook Signature Validation Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The webhook example reads the v3 signature header but shows a body-only HMAC helper described as v2 validation. Users could copy an incorrect verification pattern into production.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited section combines a v3 header with v2-style validation wording and logic. The issue affects copied implementation guidance, but it is not evidence of malicious intent.

content.value_statement: HubSpot integrations require correct authentication, object modeling, and rate limit handling. This skill provides reusable patterns for OAuth, CRM records, webhooks, and custom objects.
actual_capabilities: Generates OAuth 2.0 authorization and token refresh patterns.
Shows private app token setup for single-account integrations.
Provides contact CRUD, search, pagination, and batch operation patterns.
Explains Associations v4 linking for contacts, companies, and deals.
Outlines webhook handling with signature checks and async processing.
Covers custom object schemas and records.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, not a packaged SDK or running service.
It does not validate real HubSpot scopes, app settings, or account tier limits.
Users must adapt authentication storage, retry policy, and deployment security.
Webhook validation guidance needs review against current HubSpot documentation.

use_cases.title: Create a Public App Integration
use_cases.description: Plan OAuth scopes, token refresh, and CRM access for a multi-account HubSpot app.

use_cases.title: Automate CRM Operations
use_cases.description: Build contact, company, deal, and ticket workflows with pagination and batch operations.

use_cases.title: Model Custom HubSpot Data
use_cases.description: Design custom objects, associations, and object searches for account-specific business data.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Authentication
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new HubSpot integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose OAuth or a private app token for my HubSpot integration. Ask for app type, account count, scopes, and deployment environment.

prompt_templates.title: Build Contact Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a HubSpot contact workflow that creates, updates, searches, and paginates records. Include rate limit handling and required properties.

prompt_templates.title: Design Batch Synchronization
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a HubSpot batch synchronization plan for contacts and companies. Include chunking, partial failures, retries, and audit logging.

prompt_templates.title: Review Webhook Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my HubSpot webhook design for signature validation, replay protection, queueing, retries, and fast responses. Flag security gaps.

output_examples.input: I need contacts synced from a signup form to HubSpot.
output: Recommended authentication choice based on app ownership and account count.
A contact creation flow with required properties and duplicate handling.
Rate limit and retry guidance for production traffic.
A webhook subscription plan for relevant CRM event types.
A processing model that validates requests and queues work quickly.
Operational checks for timestamp windows, retries, and error handling.

output_examples.input: We need project records related to companies and contacts.
output: A custom object design summary with required fields and associations.
Search and update patterns for project records.
Notes about Enterprise tier requirements and object limits.

best_practices: Use OAuth for public apps and private app tokens for single-account internal tools.
Store secrets outside source control and rotate tokens on a defined schedule.
Use pagination, batch APIs, and backoff to respect HubSpot rate limits.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode HubSpot API keys, access tokens, or client secrets.
Do not process webhooks before validating signatures and timestamp freshness.
Do not loop through large record sets with individual unthrottled API calls.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build HubSpot CRM integrations with authentication, records, associations, batches, webhooks, and custom objects.

faq.question: Does it connect to HubSpot directly?
faq.answer: No. It provides implementation patterns that users adapt inside their own application code.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The examples focus on Node.js and include a small Python private app token pattern.

faq.question: Does it support OAuth?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers authorization URLs, token exchange, refresh tokens, and authenticated client creation.

faq.question: Can it help with custom objects?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes schema, record creation, reading, updating, searching, and association guidance.

faq.question: Is the webhook example production ready?
faq.answer: Review it against current HubSpot documentation before production use, especially signature validation details.
